question: Which AWS service schedules and runs large collections of independent container jobs across managed compute resources?

answers.text: AWS Batch
answers.explanation: AWS Batch plans, schedules, and runs containerized jobs across managed compute resources.

answers.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk operates web application environments rather than queues of finite processing jobs.

answers.text: Amazon ECS
answers.explanation: ECS orchestrates containers, while Batch adds job queues, job definitions, and scheduling.

answers.text: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
answers.explanation: EC2 Auto Scaling changes the number of instances in a group but has no job queue or dependency scheduler.

question: In Amazon EC2, what is an Amazon Machine Image (AMI)?

answers.text: A virtual firewall that controls instance traffic
answers.explanation: A security group is the virtual firewall. An AMI is a launch image, not a set of network rules.

answers.text: A template containing the software configuration needed to launch an instance
answers.explanation: An AMI provides operating-system and software configuration plus storage mapping information needed to launch an instance.

answers.text: A pricing commitment for a fixed amount of compute
answers.explanation: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are purchasing models and contain no machine configuration.

answers.text: A dedicated physical server for one customer
answers.explanation: A Dedicated Host is physical hardware allocated to one customer; an AMI is a reusable instance image.

answerDescription: An AMI is an EC2 launch image.

question: What is the purpose of the Traffic splitting deployment policy in an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment?

answers.text: Patch the operating system without deploying application code
answers.explanation: Managed platform updates address platform components, while traffic splitting controls an application-version deployment.

answers.text: Restart every existing instance at the same time
answers.explanation: All-at-once deployment updates all environment instances together; it does not perform a traffic evaluation.

answers.text: Update existing instances in batches
answers.explanation: Rolling deployment updates batches of existing instances. Traffic splitting uses a separate new instance set.

answers.text: Send a configured percentage of client traffic to a new application version for evaluation
answers.explanation: Traffic splitting launches new instances and directs a selected share of traffic to the new version during an evaluation period.

answerDescription: Traffic splitting evaluates a new version with a portion of production traffic.

question: Why would a Lightsail user attach a static IP address to an instance?

answers.text: To give the instance a private VPC address
answers.explanation: A Lightsail static IP is a public IPv4 address; VPC private addressing is a different network feature.

answers.text: To increase CPU and memory in the instance plan
answers.explanation: CPU and memory are selected by the Lightsail bundle. An address assignment does not change bundle resources.

answers.text: To keep a public IP address associated with the instance across a stop and start
answers.explanation: A Lightsail static IP is a fixed public address that stays associated when an instance is stopped and started.

answers.text: To store a point-in-time disk copy
answers.explanation: A snapshot stores an instance or disk copy. A static IP supplies a stable internet endpoint.

answerDescription: A static IP keeps a public endpoint stable.

question: Which AWS offering extends AWS infrastructure and services to a customer's on-premises location?

answers.text: AWS Direct Connect
answers.explanation: Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection service and does not install AWS compute infrastructure on site.

answers.text: AWS Wavelength
answers.explanation: Wavelength places AWS infrastructure in telecommunications providers' 5G networks, not customer premises.

answers.text: AWS Local Zones
answers.explanation: Local Zones are AWS-managed locations near population centers, not equipment installed in a customer data center.

answers.text: AWS Outposts
answers.explanation: AWS Outposts brings AWS infrastructure, services, APIs, and tools to a customer site while connecting to an AWS Region.

coverageObjectives: Identify AWS infrastructure deployed at a customer site

answerDescription: Outposts extends selected AWS services to on-premises locations.

question: Which statement accurately compares Amazon EC2 with AWS Elastic Beanstalk?

answers.text: EC2 only runs batch containers, while Elastic Beanstalk only runs virtual machines
answers.explanation: EC2 provides general virtual servers. AWS Batch provides the service model for queued containerized batch jobs.

answers.text: EC2 provides fixed monthly bundles, while Elastic Beanstalk supplies on-premises racks
answers.explanation: Lightsail offers fixed-resource bundles and Outposts supplies on-premises racks, so neither description fits.

answers.text: EC2 requires an Elastic Beanstalk environment before launch
answers.explanation: An EC2 instance can launch directly from an AMI; Elastic Beanstalk is not an EC2 prerequisite.

answers.text: EC2 exposes virtual-server configuration, while Elastic Beanstalk manages application environments and supporting resources
answers.explanation: EC2 gives customers instance and operating-system control. Elastic Beanstalk creates and manages resources for an application environment.

coverageObjectives: Compare EC2 control with managed application environments

answerDescription: EC2 is instance infrastructure; Elastic Beanstalk operates application environments.

question: In AWS Batch, what happens to a job whose required dependency has failed?

answers.text: The job skips its dependency and runs immediately
answers.explanation: A dependency blocks a job from becoming runnable until the prerequisite succeeds.

answers.text: The job retries after Batch removes its dependency
answers.explanation: Retry strategies retry job attempts; they do not remove failed prerequisites.

answers.text: The dependent job transitions from PENDING to FAILED
answers.explanation: Batch runs dependent jobs only after prerequisites succeed. If a dependency fails, Batch automatically moves the dependent job from PENDING to FAILED.

answers.text: The job remains RUNNABLE until capacity is available
answers.explanation: RUNNABLE means there are no outstanding dependencies; a failed dependency prevents that state.

answerDescription: A failed prerequisite fails the dependent Batch job.

question: What is the purpose of an inbound rule in an Amazon EC2 security group?

answers.text: Create a private subnet
answers.explanation: Subnets belong to a VPC and determine IP ranges. Security groups are traffic filters.

answers.text: Allow specified incoming traffic to associated resources
answers.explanation: Inbound rules define permitted protocols, ports, and sources for resources associated with the security group.

answers.text: Define the operating system for an instance launch
answers.explanation: An AMI defines the operating system and launch software configuration, not a security group.

answers.text: Set an Auto Scaling group's maximum capacity
answers.explanation: Auto Scaling capacity settings establish instance counts. Security groups filter network traffic.

coverageObjectives: Explain EC2 security group inbound rules

answerDescription: Inbound rules control permitted incoming traffic.

question: How does a rolling deployment in AWS Elastic Beanstalk update an application version?

answers.text: It uploads code without changing instances
answers.explanation: Deploying an application version changes instances according to the chosen deployment policy.

answers.text: It replaces every instance before routing requests
answers.explanation: Immutable deployment creates a new set of instances before switching; rolling deployment updates batches.

answers.text: It updates instances in batches while others serve the previous version
answers.explanation: Elastic Beanstalk divides instances into batches and updates one batch at a time while the remaining instances keep the earlier version.

answers.text: It sends a percentage of traffic to a separate new instance set
answers.explanation: Traffic splitting uses a separate temporary Auto Scaling group and evaluates a portion of traffic.

answerDescription: Rolling deployment updates a scalable environment in batches.

question: What does a snapshot of a Lightsail instance provide?

answers.text: A record of request and health metrics
answers.explanation: Metrics are operational observability data. A snapshot is for backup, recovery, and copying.

answers.text: A copy usable to create a new instance with the same configuration and data
answers.explanation: An instance snapshot captures its system disk and attached block storage disks, and can create another instance with that configuration and data.

answers.text: A fixed public address through restarts
answers.explanation: A static IP provides a stable endpoint. A snapshot is a recoverable disk and configuration copy.

answers.text: An automatic increase to a larger bundle
answers.explanation: Bundle changes resize resources; a snapshot preserves current instance state.

answerDescription: Snapshots preserve state for recovery or cloning.

question: Which statement describes an AWS Outposts rack?

answers.text: It is AWS-owned hardware installed at a customer site and connected to an AWS Region
answers.explanation: An Outposts rack is AWS-owned hardware at a customer location that extends a parent Region and requires connectivity to it.

answers.text: It is a customer-owned server managed through Systems Manager
answers.explanation: Systems Manager can manage customer-owned servers, but an Outposts rack is AWS-owned infrastructure.

answers.text: It is a dedicated private network connection to AWS
answers.explanation: Direct Connect is a networking service. An Outposts rack provides supported on-premises AWS infrastructure.

answers.text: It is an Availability Zone reserved for one customer
answers.explanation: Availability Zones are AWS regional infrastructure locations. Outposts racks are physically located at customer premises.

coverageObjectives: Distinguish an Outposts rack from network services

answerDescription: Outposts racks are AWS hardware at customer sites.

question: Which capabilities can an AWS Batch managed compute environment provide? Select TWO.

answers.text: Run customer-created ECS services on the Batch-managed cluster
answers.explanation: Batch assumes control of managed environment resources and warns against independent ECS services or tasks on its managed clusters.

answers.text: Use EC2 On-Demand or Spot capacity, or Fargate and Fargate Spot capacity
answers.explanation: Managed compute environments can use those EC2 and Fargate capacity options when configured for them.

answers.text: Manage compute capacity and instance types from specified settings
answers.explanation: In a managed compute environment, Batch manages capacity and instance types according to the settings supplied at creation.

answers.text: Guarantee all jobs remain running during scale-down
answers.explanation: Batch controls its managed resources and can terminate instances or stop tasks while managing capacity.

answerDescription: Managed environments let Batch manage configured capacity.

question: What is an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application version?

answers.text: A labeled iteration of deployable application code and configuration
answers.explanation: An application version is a labeled application iteration that points to a source bundle deployable to Elastic Beanstalk environments.

answers.text: A rolling-update policy that sets batch size
answers.explanation: Deployment policies control how a version is installed; they are environment settings, not the version artifact.

answers.text: A reusable EC2 machine image
answers.explanation: An AMI is an EC2 launch image. Elastic Beanstalk application versions are application source bundles.

answers.text: The health status of an environment and its instances
answers.explanation: Environment health reports resource status and is separate from the deployed application-version artifact.

coverageObjectives: Define an Elastic Beanstalk application version

answerDescription: Application versions are labeled deployable source bundles.

question: Which deployment-site condition is required before AWS can install an Outposts rack?

answers.text: The customer must supply EC2 instances for the rack
answers.explanation: AWS supplies and operates Outposts rack hardware; customers select supported workloads after installation.

answers.text: The site must provide required power, cooling, space, and network connectivity
answers.explanation: Outposts installation requires facility and network prerequisites including power, cooling, physical space, and parent-Region connectivity.

answers.text: A public load balancer must exist before ordering
answers.explanation: A load balancer is not an installation prerequisite; facility and network readiness are required.

answers.text: The site must be in the parent's Availability Zone
answers.explanation: Outposts is installed outside AWS Availability Zones at customer sites and extends a parent Region.

answerDescription: Outposts racks depend on site facility and network prerequisites.

question: Which statements about stopping an Amazon EBS-backed EC2 instance are true? Select TWO.

answers.text: Data on attached EBS volumes is retained
answers.explanation: Stopping does not delete attached EBS volumes, so their data persists. Delete-on-termination applies to termination, not stopping.

answers.text: An automatically assigned public IPv4 address is guaranteed to remain
answers.explanation: An automatically assigned public IPv4 address can change after stop and start; an Elastic IP supplies a stable public address.

answers.text: The instance can later be started using the same instance ID
answers.explanation: A stopped EBS-backed instance can be started again and retains its instance ID, unlike a terminated instance.

answers.text: Running-instance charges continue while stopped
answers.explanation: EC2 instance usage charges stop for an EBS-backed stopped instance, although EBS and other allocated-resource charges can continue.

answerDescription: Stopping preserves EBS-backed instance data but not an automatic public IP.

question: What occurs when a Lightsail instance is stopped and started without a static IP address?

answers.text: Its bundle changes to the next larger plan
answers.explanation: The selected bundle remains unchanged across a restart. Resizing is a separate action.

answers.text: Its default public IP address changes
answers.explanation: Lightsail assigns a new default public IP after a stopped instance starts. A static IP prevents this endpoint change.

answers.text: Its instance snapshot is automatically restored
answers.explanation: Snapshots are restored only when a user chooses that action; normal restart does not restore a snapshot.

answers.text: Its attached block storage disk is deleted
answers.explanation: Stopping and starting does not delete an attached Lightsail block storage disk; disk management is separate from the public IP.

coverageObjectives: Recognize Lightsail public IP restart limitation

answerDescription: A static IP retains a Lightsail public endpoint through restart.
